properties.description: Keep every Decision's unchosen options as forkable siblings; re-open a past decision at its epoch and take a different branch, with the alternative's consequence design computed by replay (propagate/compare) rather than pre-stored. Selection of which fork to expand follows the reward signal — defects and field trials — not the whole tree; the human does the credit assignment. The navigation layer of reflow2-as-decision-MDP, unifying BL-70 (branches), BL-80 (merge, how a road comes home) and BL-44 (claims). DESIGNED 2026-07-24: the fork point is a coordinate, decision → AT_EPOCH → epoch.checksum → the committed export (dec:fork-point-address), so no ref/DAG layer is needed; re-opening mints a superseding Decision rather than un-accepting the original (dec:reopen-supersedes); the epoch chain the whole thing addresses is backfilled from real release tags (dec:temporal-backfill-from-releases). BUILT 2026-09-23 on Anthony's rulings (dec:step-4-fork-point-finds-its-address-in-git-and-reopen-is-one-call). `fork_point` (core DesignGraph::fork_point, crates/reflow2-core/src/fork.rs) resolves a Decision to its epoch and export checksum, what it GOVERNS, the ChangeEvents at LATER epochs touching those (null — "cannot tell", not "none" — when unpinned), the doubt evidence behind it and `held_up`, registered alternatives, and whether it is already re-opened. Measured first: only 37 of 454 accepted decisions carry AT_EPOCH, so an unpinned decision's address is found in git (crates/reflow2-mcp/src/git.rs earliest_export_containing): the first first-parent commit whose committed export holds the id, with that export's content_hash and a `git:<commit>:<path>` location — reported as EARLIEST EVIDENCE, never as when it was decided; bisected (~11 reads, ~3.5 s) because a pickaxe search measured 36 s. Verified on the real repo: the stamp decision resolves to #572's merge commit with #572's exact export hash. `reopen_choice` (core reopen_decision) applies dec:reopen-supersedes in one call: a new proposed Decision that OBSOLETES the original, which stays accepted and untouched, with the road taken registered as the first alternative when its location is passed; refuses a non-accepted original, an existing id, and an original already re-opened by one still open. The revise-design skill routes a change of mind about a settled decision through these two and forbids flipping it back to proposed. The merge that brings a road home remains apply_merge with the fork point as base.
properties.name: Hold and re-fork a decision's unchosen alternatives
